summary: Verifiable webhook watermark and SIEM ingest validation for tenant audit stream
description: Customer requests a verifiable delivery proof for tenant-scoped webhook audit stream plus a small SIEM ingest validation harness. They want per-batch watermarks, signed delivery nonces, and a sample of the canonicalized payloads used for SIEM mapping to satisfy an external security audit. Current delivery is working but customer needs artifacts and a short test run to validate their SIEM mapping and evidence chain.
impact: Customer must provide compliance artifacts to their auditor next week. No production outage; primary need is cryptographic provenance and a deterministic sample for SIEM mapping. If delayed, audit may request extension causing legal overhead.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer subscribes to tenant audit webhook with mutual TLS and confirms delivery URL
2) Customer receives audit events but requests signed-watermark headers on each batch and a manifest that proves ordering
3) Customer wants a 1-hour sample where Redwood produces a Merkle checkpoint and per-event compact signature for validation by their SIEM ingestion team
investigation_notes: Initial triage: webhook handshakes succeed; no 5xx spikes recorded in window. Delivery pipeline annotates X-Redwood-Watermark and X-Redwood-Nonce headers but customer needs header payload to include compact signature and merkle checkpoint reference.
Hypothesis: signing step runs in separate process and manifest generation is gated by hourly checkpoint job; customer requested per-batch manifest which differs from our hourly checkpoint cadence.

Validated: signing service supports compact signatures (RFC 8037 style) and KMS key policy allows tenant-scoped signatures. Need to add manifest per-batch and include proof-of-order (sequence and prev_hash).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Opening ticket after security review call. Customer provided SIEM field mapping and sample of expected event shape.
2026-03-10 - Marco Liu (Eng): Confirmed KMS signing capability and located producer job. Will implement per-batch manifest in shipper; ETA for dev change 2026-03-12.

2026-03-11 - Customer (GreenScale Health - Naomi Ortiz): Confirmed that sample payloads must include original headers and full UTF-8 event bodies. Auditor also requested HMAC of concatenated tenant_id+batch_id as quick proof.

2026-03-12 - Marco Liu (Eng): Deployed a canary that emits X-Redwood-Watermark, X-Redwood-Nonce, X-Redwood-Sig and a manifest object to S3. Running a 1-hour sample run now; will upload artifacts when complete.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided: enabled per-batch signed manifest in canary and uploaded three artifact files to customer's secure share. Manifest includes merkle_root, prev_hash, batch_seq, and compact signature header values.

Permanent fix: shipper will be updated to emit per-batch manifests by default for tenant-level webhook exports and include HMAC quick-proof header for auditor workflows. Change will be rolled out to dedicated region via canary + feature flag.

Follow-ups: document the header specification in Confluence (link below), add automated SIEM ingest test to CI that validates canonicalization and field mappings, and schedule a short knowledge-transfer session with customer security on 2026-03-16.
